top.title: Bobby Durkin hits game-winner to beat Cincinnati 63-61
top.description: CINCINNATI, OH - NOVEMBER 09: Minnesota Golden Gophers forward Bobby Durkin (3) reacts with his teammates after making a game-winning three-pointer during the game against the Minnesota Golden Gophers and the Cincinnati Bearcats on November 9, 2026 at Fifth Third Arena in Cincinnati, OH. (Photo by Ian Johnson/Icon Sportswire via Getty Images) | Icon Sportswire via Getty Images After trailing for most of the second half, the Gophers scrambled to come back and Bobby Durkin hit a deep three in the final seconds to beat the Cincinnati Bearcats 63-61 and remain undefeated. Kyan Evans did most of the work throughout the game, scoring 26 points, grabbing 10 rebounds and five assists. But it was Isaac Asuma, advancing the ball to Bobby Durkin, who hit his only three of the game to give Minnesota the lead with 0.4 on the clock and essentially sealing the win for Minnesota. Minnesota jumped out to an early lead and seemed to be controlling the game for the first 10 minutes of the game. But then Cincinnati just slowly took control of the pace of the game, playing good defense and making things difficult for everyone on the Gopher offense except Evans. The Bearcats forced a ton of Gopher turnovers that they turned into points, but Minnesota battled back and Durkin put the nail in the coffin to push the Gophers to 3-0 on the young season. WHY IT MATTERED: The win is great, being 3-0 is great, but this will count as a Quad 1 win for the Gophers and is the best non-conference win since beating North Carolina and West Virginia in back-to-back games in 2011. This is a game that will benefit the Gophers as they try to get back to the NCAA Tournament. GAME BALL: Evans had a double-double and his first big night scoring as a Gopher. But how do you not give the game ball to Bobby Buckets? THE STAT : For Cincinnati, it was turnovers; for the Gophers, it was offensive rebounds. Both were garnering extra possessions for their team and frustrating their fans. Cincy forced 17 turnovers that resulted in 16 points. Minnesota grabbed 13 offensive rebounds that allowed them to score 11 bonus points. TURNING POINT : This one was definitely in favor of the Bearcats, with a 79% chance of winning with 17 seconds left. And then MJ Collins missed the front end of a 1-and-1 and Asuma found Durkin for the game-winner. HOT : Cincinnati’s Tylen Riley has scored 11 points this season, but he was on fire tonight. The senior guard was 8/17 and 6/9 from three to finish with 25 points. NOT : Durkin had just two points and was 0-5 from three this game before he hit the game-winner. He had two threes blocked and looked out-of-sorts for most of this game. UP NEXT: The Gophers get a couple of gimme-games with Southern and Western Illinois coming to the Barn before three straight games against Power 5 teams. Southern is on Thursday at 7:00.

top.title: Purdue Uses a 21-2 Run to Blow By Illinois State: 76-59
top.description: WEST LAFAYETTE, IN - NOVEMBER 09: Purdue Boilermakers guard Antione West Jr. (1) looks to pass while defined by Illinois State Redbirds guard Mason Klabo (3) in the first half of play during a men's college basketball game between the Illinois State Redbirds vs the Purdue Boilermakers on November 09, 2026 at Mackey Arena in West Lafayette, IN. (Photo by Jeffrey Brown/Icon Sportswire via Getty Images) | Icon Sportswire via Getty Images Purdue came into this game looking to avoid their first 0-3 start since the 1950-1951 season. A season in which they finished 8-14 and 4-10 in conference play. Standing in their way was an Illinois State team from The Valley. Purdue changes up the starting lineup as you would expect with Antione West Jr. and Jack Benter being slotted in place of Omer Mayer and Gicarri Harris. The writing was on the wall with that one given the substitution pattern you saw in the two overtimes from the game against Valparaiso. John Wooden Memorial Player of the Game (JWMPOTG): Giving this one to Antione West Jr. in what I hope is his coming out party. The redshirt freshman went 7-11 from the floor including 3-4 from three and helped spark the run that put this game out of reach. Purdue needed to do a number of things to return a little bit of hope to the fanbase. First and foremost they needed to win. That’s always number one. Second though, they needed to shoot the ball better, show better effort on defense, and maybe, just maybe, play a full 40 minutes. If Buddy the Elf can recharge in just 40 minutes there’s no reason that this Purdue men’s basketball team can’t play a good 40 minutes of basketball. While Purdue looked better in the first half than they did the last 30 minutes we saw them play, the second half and double overtime against Valparaiso, they still had plenty of problems. Purdue’s offense too often resulted in clumps of players around the perimeter just sort of standing there. That’s no way to run an offense. Purdue was also incredibly streaky in the first half. At one point they hit seven shots in a row. Then, toward the end of the half they went 1-9. I won’t say it was feast or famine because what we watched was no feast. Purdue did shoot the three better in the first half but that might be partly because they shot far fewer. In the first half they went 4/10 from three. West hit two threes while Benter and Jacobsen added one a piece. Yes, Jacobsen. He was again Purdue’s leading scorer heading into halftime as the only Boilermaker in double figures with 10. On defense the Boilermakers did a good job handling the Redbirds three point shooting. They came into this game shooting just over 50% from three in their first two games. In the first half of this one Purdue held them to 3-16 from three with one of those made threes being a bank in off the glass. Despite these good numbers on defense Illinois State continued to chip away at the lead. Purdue never looked comfortable out there and went into half with a smaller lead

top.title: Finally, Purdue basketball finds its offense late to run off Illinois State
top.description: WEST LAFAYETTE − At last, Purdue basketball fans can breathe a sigh of relief. It took huge late run to blow the game open, but the Boilermakers left Mackey Arena with their first victory. A lineup change that included Jack Benter and Antione West Jr. among the starting helped pilot Purdue 's 76-59 win over Illinois State . Purdue (1-2) led 50-48 midway through the second half before landing the knockout blow it needed after losses to Gonzaga and Valparaiso to open the season while also snapping out of its 3-point shooting funk. After combining to shoot just 20.4% from 3 in the first two games, the Boilers made 8 of 19 against the Redbirds (1-2). Purdue basketball turning point vs. Illinois State Despite a hot shooting first half, Purdue couldn't separate itself from the Redbirds. Illinois State had a chance to cut the lead to two Louie Semona II's 3-pointer was off and Enzo Shahrvin pulled down the rebound. Purdue called timeout to set up a final play. Antione West Jr. ended up making a stepback 3-pointer from the right wing to give the Boilermakers a 36-28 halftime lead. That shot was Purdue's saving grace for a long time, but it was just enough to keep Illinois State from ever pulling even or going ahead. Eventually, Purdue found its footing and blew the game open with a 24-2 run relying on a lineup of Antione West Jr., Luke Ertel, CJ Cox, Jack Benter and Daniel Jacobsen. Game MVP Jack Benter received his first two career starts out of necessity when Trey Kaufman-Renn was sidelined to open last season. On Monday, the junior was in the starting rotation for the first time in a year. He showed what he's capable of from the get go, sinking a 3-pointer for the game's first points, then drawing a charge on the defensive end. It set the stage for a productive night across the board for Benter, who finished with 14 points, 5 rebounds, 3 assists and a steal. 3 Purdue basketball standouts vs. Illinois State Daniel Jacobsen: Three games in a row is a trend. The 7-foot-4 center is Purdue's best offensive piece. It was another stellar night for the Boilermaker big man, contributing his third straight game with at least 20 points, hitting that number on the nose. Jacobsen also had 7 rebounds and 3 assists. Antione West Jr.: In his first career start after sitting out last season, West had a coming out party. West scored 17 points on 7 of 11 shooting and added 2 rebounds, 2 assists and a steal. CJ Cox: The junior guard made three early midrange jumpers. He didn't fill up the stat sheet, but he didn't hurt the Boilermakers either. Cox had 10 points, 3 assists and, in typical Cox fashion, no turnovers. Sam King covers sports for the Journal & Courier. Email him at sking@jconline.com and follow him on X and Instagram @samueltking. top.title: Dana White Turns Down Donald Trump’s Press Secretary Offer in Hilarious Exchange at White House
top.description: So, the real-life episode of The Office continues. Just two days after Donald Trump jokingly offered him the role of press secretary in his administration, Dana White made a personal appearance at the White House. For the unversed, the President had taken to his Truth Social account to announce that the UFC CEO and several other fighters were welcome to join his cabinet. However, just a day after the announcement, Trump clarified that the offer was made in a jovial spirit and that he was only joking. While he maintained that White would be a fantastic choice for the position, he insisted that there was nothing serious behind the proposal. The UFC CEO had confirmed that he would meet Trump on November 9 after returning to the United States from the Zuffa Boxing 12 event in London. However, the President later clarified that White’s visit had nothing to do with the press secretary offer. According to Trump, the UFC boss was already planning to be in Washington and had simply decided to stop by and see him. And that is exactly what White ended up doing. During the November 9 White House news conference alongside Trump, White officially turned down the prospect of becoming press secretary. While admitting that he doesn’t say no to the President, the UFC CEO made it clear that he had no interest in entering politics at the moment. He said, “I don’t tell the president no to anything. I didn’t say no. Literally every media outlet was calling me, and I didn’t want to be disrespectful and say anything until he said something first.” Dana White appeared at the White House press briefing podium Monday after President Trump said he had offered the UFC CEO the open press secretary role, only to reveal a day later that he “was kidding.” “I have zero political aspirations,” White told reporters. https://t.co/6bq23p0XvK — CBS News (@CBSNews) November 9, 2026 ALSO READ: Justin Gaethje vs. Ilia Topuria 2 Will Never Happen, Ali Abdelaziz Makes Bold Claim Trump then added to the bizarre nature of the situation by reiterating that he had been joking about the entire proposition. He said, “We were having a very bad press day, and I don’t know why, I thought of his name; he’s been a friend for a long time. I said I think I’m going to get Dana White to be my new press secretary. I said it to a group of the press, and that was it. I was sort of kidding.” The President further explained, “Then they wrote the stories as though I wasn’t kidding, and then [Dana] was inundated and I was inundated. top.description: USA TODAY Network via Reuters Connect President Donald Trump has been pushing for a Pete Rose pardon for more than a year now. And on Monday, he made it clear that he still hasn’t given up on the idea. During a White House press briefing alongside UFC CEO Dana White, Trump said that he “would give Pete Rose a pardon” for the tax charges that the late MLB hits leader pleaded guilty to in 1990. Trump also insisted that the former Cincinnati Reds star had been “very mistreated” by baseball and said that Rose deserved to be in the Hall of Fame “a long time ago.” Pete Rose’s Long Saga Rose finished his career with 4,256 hits, the most in MLB history. But he was banned from baseball in 1989 after an investigation found that he had bet on games, including Reds games, while managing the team. A year later, Rose pleaded guilty to two felony counts of filing false federal income tax returns after underreporting more than $300,000 in income from appearances, autograph sessions, memorabilia sales, and gambling winnings. He served five months in federal prison. Rose’s lifetime ban kept him off the Hall of Fame ballot for decades, and his requests to be reinstated were repeatedly denied, as was his request for the Hall to reconsider . He died in September 2024 at the age of 83. In March 2025, Trump announced on Truth Social that he would be “signing a complete pardon” for Rose. Two months later, commissioner Rob Manfred removed Rose from MLB’s permanently ineligible list, though his earliest chance at the Hall of Fame is the Classic Baseball Era Committee ballot in December 2027, per ESPN . ’40 years of hell’ On Monday, White was at the White House taking questions from reporters after Trump claimed he was “only kidding” about making him press secretary. When one reporter brought up Trump’s potential Rose pardon, White said that he supported it. “I don’t advise the president on anything ever, but yeah, I think it’s fair. top.title: 3 notes from Indiana women’s basketball’s 84-56 win over Bradley
top.description: BLOOMINGTON, IN - NOVEMBER 03: Indiana Hoosiers head coach Teri Moren with the high five in the second half of play during a women's college basketball game between Florida Gulf Coast Eagles vs the Indiana Hoosiers on November 03, 2026 at Simon Skjodt Assembly Hall in Bloomington, IN. (Photo by Jeffrey Brown/Icon Sportswire via Getty Images) | Icon Sportswire via Getty Images Indiana women’s basketball beat Bradley 84-56 on Monday night at Assembly Hall in Bloomington. The win brings the Hoosiers to 3-0 on the season with a few more matchups to come before they face their first real test against Mississippi State toward the end of the month. All three have given Indiana things to feel good about, and Monday’s win was no different. Here’s a few observations: Taking control in the second quarter Indiana actually entered the second quarter with an 18-15 deficit. The Hoosiers shot poorly from all over the court while the Braves did enough on the interior to pull ahead. Bradley’s an interesting team to go against, as Teri Moren explained after the game. The Braves run a ton of movement on offense and Moren was eager to see how her roster responded to such a different challenge after two dominant wins to open the season. The Hoosiers responded alright, winning the second quarter 27-8 while dominating the glass to surge ahead for a lead they’d never relinquish. Malia Samuels was vital, going 4-4 from the field while pulling down a pair of rebounds and logging an assist. Indiana’s been capable of really hitting the gas under Moren and this team is showing it can have that gear early on. Maya Makalusky making an impact Makalusky, a second-year forward, performed well all over the court in leading Indiana with 16 points on the night. She finished shooting 4-6 from 3-point range while tying for second on the team in rebounding with five. Indiana’s going to need more nights like this from Makalusky, who committed years ago as the top prospect in the state. Her overall skillset fits well into what Moren likes to do on both ends of the floor, so it’s all about developing into that role. Lenee Beaumont Indiana was without Lenee Beaumont, its on-court leader, who left the game in the second quarter after seeming to tweak something in her leg after getting into the paint. She remained on the bench with the team, however. Moren shared after the game that Beaumont hyperextended her knee and that, while she’ll get everything looked at tomorrow, the program is hopeful for good news. #iuwbb head coach Teri Moren’s opening statement (and update on Lenée Beaumont) after a 84-56 win over Bradley: pic.twitter.com/6np7yBf2Sj — Sean McAvoy (@sean_mc07) November 10, 2026 Join the conversation! top.title: Cisco to link all future products to its SaaS-y Cloud Control management tool
top.description: Cisco will no longer create products that don’t integrate with Cloud Control, its SaaS-y management platform that offers netadmins a single tool to manage all of the networking giant’s devices and much of its software portfolio. The networking giant announced Cloud Control in June 2025 and only made it available to customers in the USA. Cisco has previously told The Register that slow rollout reflects the fact that Cisco needs to nail privacy and other regulatory niceties, and deploy infrastructure, before introducing the service to other markets. It appears Cisco is now satisfied it has sorted out those issues. Jeff Schultz, Cisco’s senior vice president for portfolio strategy and marketing, today told the company’s Live conference in Australia that Cloud Control will come online in the European Union, UK, and Down Under in February 2027. Japan, India, and Canada will get their turn in May. Schultz said Cisco is “working tirelessly” to deploy Cloud Control across the world as soon as possible. He also revealed that, starting next year, Cisco will no longer ship products that don’t integrate with Cloud Control. That doesn’t mean those products will be manageable only if they can connect to Cloud Control. Instead, the decision reflects Cisco’s belief that the main thing stopping its customers buying more of its products is the complexity of operating them in concert. Schultz also feels that Cloud Control represents “platform advantage” for Cisco, because when users integrate networking, security, and observability the result is better manageability and resilience. Schultz also told the conference that Cisco will bundle its Thousand Eyes observability and security tool with the “Essentials” and “Advantage” licenses. “We admit it was hard to license and deploy,” he said during his keynote speech, adding that the tool will be deployed automatically with Wi‑Fi 6E and Wi‑Fi 7 hardware. Another product Cisco plans to bring to more customers is Live Protect, a tool that implements compensating controls for flaws that organizations can’t immediately patch. Live Protect currently works on some switches, plus SD-WAN and WLAN controllers. From December, Cisco will extend it to 8000 series routers, secure firewalls, campus gateway, and to Cloud Control itself. From May 2027, Live Protect will work with Cisco’s ASR 9000 series service aggregation routers and Network Convergence System. ®

Bills Had Shot at Odell Beckham More Than a Decade Ago The Bills famously had a chance to land Odell Beckham Jr., who came into the NFL as a first-round pick of the New York Giants in 2014. top.title: Josh Allen has run for 5,000 yards and only 4 other QBs can say that
top.description: MINNEAPOLIS, MINNESOTA - NOVEMBER 09: Josh Allen #17 of the Buffalo Bills runs the ball for a first down against the Minnesota Vikings during the first quarter of the game at U.S. Bank Stadium on November 09, 2026 in Minneapolis, Minnesota. (Photo by Stephen Maturen/Getty Images) | Getty Images Josh Allen has run for 5,000 yards in the NFL. For a guy whose primary job is throwing the football, that’s a lot of ground covered. The Buffalo Bills quarterback became just the fifth quarterback in NFL history to reach that total during Buffalo’s Week 9 game against the Minnesota Vikings. Allen crossed the 5k mark in the third quarter on a series of designed runs. He entered the game at 4991 then had a 7-yard run in the first quarter to get to 4998. He lost one yard on the kneel down to end the first half to fall back to 4997. A 5-yard scramble from the Minnesota 21 was followed by a 3-yard run to make sure he was over. And counting… Allen joins Lamar Jackson, Michael Vick, Cam Newton, and Russell Wilson in the 5,000-yard group. That’s the entire list, and Allen has put himself on it in his ninth NFL season. Bills fans have watched those yards come a few different ways. There have been scrambles after the protection breaks down, designed runs, and more than a few plays where Allen decides the best way to get a first down is to go through whoever is standing in front of him. They all count. Of course, if he slid more often, like we all keep screaming for him to do, it would have taken a few more carries to get there. Allen already owns the NFL record for career rushing touchdowns by a quarterback. Now he has another number to go with it, and another reminder of how much of Buffalo’s offense has come from his legs.

nigeria.title: Canada makes rural immigration programme permanent
nigeria.description: By Favour Ulebor Canada has made its Rural Community Immigration Pilot a permanent programme to attract and retain skilled foreign workers in smaller communities facing persistent labour shortages. The Minister of Immigration, Refugees and Citizenship, Lena Metlege Diab, announced the decision on Monday, November 9, 2026, in Pictou County, Nova Scotia. According to a statement published on the website of Immigration, Refugees and Citizenship Canada (IRCC), the programme will initially retain the 14 communities currently participating in the pilot, with plans to expand to more communities in the future. The employer- and community-driven programme is designed to address labour shortages in rural areas by connecting skilled foreign workers and their families with employers and community support services. It also seeks to encourage newcomers to settle permanently in smaller communities and contribute to their economic development. Speaking during the announcement, Diab said the government recognised the critical role rural communities played in Canada’s economy despite the challenges they faced in attracting workers. “Our government understands that rural communities play a critical role in powering Canada’s economy. Under Canada’s 2027–2029 Immigration Levels Plan, the government has allocated 5,500 admission spaces to the permanent Rural Community Immigration Program. The government said the initiative was part of its broader immigration policy aimed at stabilising the number of immigrants admitted into the country, reducing the temporary resident population and retaining skilled foreign workers already contributing to local communities. It added that preliminary results from the pilot showed that foreign workers had helped address labour shortages in critical sectors, including healthcare, education, sales and services, between 2025 and 2026. The department also disclosed that participating communities had vetted and designated more than 1,950 trusted employers experiencing persistent labour shortages that could not be addressed through the local workforce between January 2025 and August 2026. nigeria.title: I’m a godfather, but I don’t impose appointments on governors — Osoba
nigeria.description: By Efe Onodjae Former Ogun State Governor, Olusegun Osoba has defended the role of political godfathers in Nigeria’s democracy, saying their responsibility should be to offer advice and guidance rather than impose political appointees on elected governors. Osoba, who spoke during a podcast hosted by Reuben Abati and shared on X (formerly Twitter), said he considered himself a political godfather but had deliberately avoided interfering in the administration of his political successors. According to him, he had never nominated anyone for appointment as commissioner, special adviser, councillor or local government chairman in the state. He said: “I agree, I’m a godfather. But one thing that is working for me in my state is that I hardly interfere. I counsel and advise him. I have never nominated one person into his government.” Explaining his position, the former governor said imposing candidates on an administration could undermine the governor’s authority and create unnecessary divisions among his political supporters. He noted that appointing one person from the numerous people around him could offend others, while anyone recommended by him might be viewed with suspicion within the administration. Osoba recalled that during his tenure as governor, he adopted a system that allowed each federal constituency to nominate candidates for commissioner positions. He said he requested one name from each federal constituency and subsequently reviewed their credentials before assigning them portfolios, adding that the approach helped him avoid pressure from political associates. The former governor maintained that political godfathers should ensure that people who worked for a candidate during electioneering campaigns were recognised and compensated, but should not dictate how an elected governor runs his administration. “That’s the role of a godfather. I agree, I’m a godfather,” he said. Osoba also defended the participation of experienced elders in candidate selection, citing his support for a presidential candidate whom he described as experienced, having served in the Lagos State House of Assembly, House of Representatives and Senate, as well as in the corporate sector. Tyler Robinson, 23, faces a potential death penalty for allegedly killing Kirk with a gunshot to the neck on a university campus in the western US state of Utah on September 10, 2025. The killing of Kirk at age 31 at an event planned by his right-wing youth organization, Turning Point, sent shockwaves through the US political world. Kirk had become a popular leader in a Christian Nationalist movement that preaches traditional values while voicing intolerance for diversity and LGBTQ communities. Turning Point was key to mobilizing youth support for Donald Trump’s re-election as president in 2024. The group is now led by his wife, Erika Kirk. The prosecution had sought a trial as early as January 2028, while Robinson’s lawyers had wanted until the end of 2029 to prepare their defense. Last month, Trump criticized the judge and said the case “should be tried within a month, not three years.” Kirk’s assassination last year triggered a 33-hour manhunt culminating in Robinson surrendering to authorities. He has pled not guilty. The prosecution has presented text messages in which Robinson confessed to planning the murder to his roommate, a transgender person with whom they allege Robinson was in a relationship. The defense has focused on alleged weaknesses in the DNA and ballistic evidence. nigeria.title: Manchester United are becoming a club of survival rather than ambition
nigeria.description: The 4-4 draw against Aston Villa felt like a victory at Old Trafford, but the fact that supporters could celebrate a point while their club sits in the relegation zone tells a more troubling story about how far United’s expectations have fallen. There was a time when a draw at Old Trafford felt like a defeat. Manchester United were a club built around winning, where anything short of three points could leave supporters disappointed, regardless of the performance. The expectation was not simply to compete but to dominate, to set the standards and to make winning feel like an obligation. Those expectations seem increasingly distant. On Sunday, Manchester United celebrated a 4-4 draw against Aston Villa with the sort of emotion usually reserved for a significant victory. Two goals in stoppage time, courtesy of Joshua Zirkzee and Patrick Dorgu, rescued a point after Michael Carrick’s side had twice fallen two goals behind. The comeback was extraordinary, the atmosphere was electric and the players had every reason to appreciate their resilience. But perhaps the most revealing aspect of the afternoon was not the comeback itself. It was how much it meant. Manchester United are now in a position where avoiding defeat feels like an achievement. A point against Aston Villa, under ordinary circumstances, would hardly have been considered a successful afternoon for a club of United’s stature. Yet the circumstances have become so desperate that the draw felt like a victory. That is how quickly footballing standards can collapse. United sit 18th in the Premier League with eight points from 10 matches . They have managed just one league victory, recorded against Ipswich Town in August, and Sunday’s result extended their winless league run to eight matches. It is a club-record sequence in the Premier League. The numbers are alarming, but the deeper concern is what they reveal about the club’s changing relationship with success. Manchester United have become a team defined by what they are trying to avoid rather than what they are trying to achieve. Instead of discussing title challenges, European qualification or the development of a convincing footballing identity, the conversation increasingly revolves around managerial uncertainty, defensive mistakes, relegation calculations and the possibility of another disappointing weekend. Survival has become the immediate ambition. And that is a remarkable development for a club whose history was built on refusing to accept anything less than excellence. nigeria.description: A 56-year-old civil servant in the United Kingdom, UK, Kashim Chowdhury has been convicted of nine counts of fraud after secretly holding multiple full-time government jobs and fraudulently earning more than £284,000 in taxpayers’ money. Chowdhury, from east London, held five overlapping government positions in the spring of 2023, concealing his multiple employment arrangements from the departments that hired him. After seven hours of deliberation, a jury unanimously found him guilty of eight counts of fraud by false representation and one count of fraud by failure to disclose. The prosecution accused Chowdhury of “deliberate, intentional dishonesty” and “exploiting the system” to secure multiple salaries from public sector employers. During the proceedings, the judge said Chowdhury faced a “very significant custodial sentence”. He also refused him bail, citing the seriousness of the offences and Chowdhury’s own wellbeing. Sarah Melo, a specialist prosecutor at the Crown Prosecution Service (CPS) Serious Economic Organised Crime and International Directorate, described his actions as sustained dishonesty. “This was sustained and deliberate dishonesty,” Melo said. “He knew he could not legitimately hold multiple full-time positions at the same time, but continued to conceal what he was doing.” A spokesperson for the Department for Environment, Food and Rural Affairs (Defra) said Chowdhury had “abused the trust placed in him as a public servant”. The department added that it would use all available avenues to recover the proceeds of his offending. Between 2020 and 2023, Chowdhury held eight overlapping full-time public sector positions and earned a total of £350,000, according to evidence presented in court. Prosecutors told the court that he provided inaccurate information about his employment status on job application forms and failed to disclose to government departments that he was already employed as a civil servant. After securing the positions, he also failed to inform his employers that he was working for other government departments. Chowdhury was permitted to work entirely from home after telling his employers he was caring for his mother, with whom he lived in east London. His mother had dementia and was diagnosed with terminal cancer in 2023. However, rather than reduce his workload to care for her, he continued taking on additional government positions. In the spring of 2023, he held positions across the Department for Environment, Food and Rural Affairs, the Department of Health and Social Care, the UK Health Security Agency (UKHSA), the Department for Business and Trade, the Food Standards Agency and the Home Office. About 117,000 NEAR, or roughly $430,000, passed through the six tokens, Elliptic wrote . The trail sits inside the broader laundering of the Oct. 29 Binance theft, which the exchange has put at $6.34 billion and which the FBI has attributed to North Korea’s TraderTraitor group. entertainment.title: Nkanyeziyethu Malunga: The Zimbabwean Designer Preserving African Heritage Through Fashion
entertainment.description: At her workshop in Bulawayo, Zimbabwe, Nkanyeziyethu Malunga crafted colour into fabric, using plants, tree bark and other natural materials gathered from the environment. Choosing a colour or designing a pattern is only one of the processes. Each material carries details on how it was gathered, prepared, and transformed, which Malunga is incorporating into contemporary fashion. “My dyes are mainly extracted from plants such as mnyii and hibiscus. Although I also use many other plants, including tubers, that have properties suitable for dye extraction. I love hibiscus not only for its petals, which produce beautiful dyes, but also for its tea.” The 37-year-old designer is challenging conventional notions about what defines a fashion collection and where creative knowledge originates. Through her clothing business, GANU, she transforms indigenous materials and skills into clothes and accessories, demonstrating how knowledge passed down through generations can inform modern design, provide opportunities for rural women, and conserve cultural practices. Her method is based on teachings learned from her late maternal grandmother, Ngatsha Nkatha, who resided in Tsholotsho, a rural district in Zimbabwe. During the school vacations, Malunga and her siblings traveled from Bulawayo to visit grandma, witnessing as she turned sisal, sedge, and reeds into winnowing baskets. “When I was a child, I often visited my grandmother in the village with my siblings. She was very dexterous with her fingers, and that passion eventually became mutual.” Malunga started experimenting with fashion in her teens before launching Ganu in 2013. The name is derived from iganu, the Ndebele term for marula fruit, and represents her connection to local resources and African identity. Her creations blend basketry, crocheting, batik, and beadwork with natural dyes, leather, and other locally produced materials. For Malunga, the importance of these materials goes beyond their appearance. Bamboo, sisal, reeds, and sedge are used in basketry, and she breeds Angora goats for their fur, which she straightens and dyes to make garments. Cowhide obtained from local abattoirs is softened in a tannery before being mixed into leather designs. “I keep Angora goats for the fur needed in garment production. However, for raw materials such as cowhide, I usually source these from local abattoirs while sisal and tree barks are either harvested by me or sometimes extracted by colleagues I work with, who are based in the rural areas.” Desmond Ntini , a cultural entrepreneur based in Bulawayo, sees Malunga’s work as part of a broader shift in how African history is perceived and used. ” Malunga is redefining the fashion industry by blending traditional African influences with contemporary creativity. entertainment.title: Israel Olaleye: What Selling Land Taught Me About How Nigerians Think About Money
entertainment.description: In 2021, I graduated from the University of Ibadan with a degree in Mathematics. I thought my life would be about numbers on a whiteboard. I did not know it would become about numbers in people’s bank accounts, and the fears, hopes and contradictions that sit behind them. By mid-2023, I had taken a job selling real estate. I started at the very bottom, as a sales development representative: the person who makes the first call, sends the message and follows up when nobody replies. Today, I manage a sales team. Somewhere between then and now, I stopped seeing real estate as a business of land and buildings. I started seeing it as a mirror. Put a property in front of a Nigerian, and you will learn, very quickly, how they think about money. Here is some of what that mirror has shown me: A prospect once told me, with complete confidence, “I have my money ready for the land.” We fixed an inspection. We walked the site together under the afternoon sun, red earth on our shoes. Then, standing on the plot, the prospect asked if they could pay next year. I was not angry. I understood. Saying “I am ready” feels good. Being ready is different. It means you have decided what the money is for, and you are willing to let it go. I have seen versions of that moment many times. The client who books an inspection for 2 pm and is still not there at 4 pm. The person who asks for options, receives ten properties that match exactly what they requested, and replies, “Do you have something else?” The buyer who is ready until it is time to decide, and then needs three more months to think. The one who disappeared after asking for a price came back after the price went up, and asked for the old price. For a long time, these moments frustrated me. But they taught me that most people do not have a money problem. They have a decision problem. We are a generation that earns, spends, plans and postpones, often all at the same time. You can earn a lot and still not be wealthy One idea I keep returning to is that you can earn twenty million naira a year and still not be wealthy. Income is what comes in. Wealth is what stays and grows. Two people can earn the same salary and end up in completely different places ten years later, simply because one converted part of that income into assets and the other converted all of it into lifestyle. Wealthy people do not always look wealthy. Some of the most financially secure people I have met do not drive the loudest cars. entertainment.description: Some people spend years trying to avoid awkward situations. Seyi Ademeso has built a career out of creating them, in the identity of Meshkiey . The content creator has turned everyday social discomfort into a distinctive style of comedy, earning an audience that recognises him for his unconventional approach to skits. But there is more to Seyi than the character who seems willing to embarrass himself for a laugh. Beyond the camera, he is a creative strategist, entrepreneur and businessman with ambitions that stretch far beyond social media. I think I’ve always been a very observant person. Even growing up, I noticed little things about people, the way they behaved, the way they spoke, the funny things people did without realising they were funny. I was also quite expressive. I wouldn’t necessarily say I was the loudest person in every room, but I definitely had a personality. I liked making people laugh, and I enjoyed doing things differently. Looking back, I think a lot of the things people now associate with Meshkiey were actually already there. The difference is that I eventually found a platform where I could turn those traits into something creative. When did you start creating, really? entertainment.title: From the Sky to the Earth To You: Earth & Sky by Banke Kuku
entertainment.description: With Earth & Sky , her Spring/Summer 2027 collection, Banke Kuku turns to nature’s most essential cycle: the sky gives rain, the rain feeds the earth, and the earth gives back. Reimagining the water cycle as a circle of life, the collection celebrates the abundance that flows from it. Earth & Sky is built around seven prints in three families. The Sky family is led by the hero print, Bougainvillea Sky, with watercolour bougainvillea, bees, butterflies and birds drifting across a turquoise ground, alongside Dove Sky and Daybreak Sky. The Earth family, Yellow Trumpet and Flower Bud, draws on flowering plants such as Costus spectabilis . The Rain family pairs Raindrop, a glossy, near-photographic print set against the softness of the watercolours, with the Kuku Monogram in fresh colourways. Sky prints are finished with hand-embroidered clouds and raindrops on flowing kaftans and kimono robes. Speaking on the inspiration, Creative Director Banke Kuku shares: “I never start with a sketch. I start with a feeling, and for Earth & Sky, that feeling was abundance. This year I became a mother for the first time, and everywhere I looked, nature was reflecting that same fullness back at me. This is my most personal collection.” A CYCLE OF GIVING BACK In nature, nothing is wasted, and everything returns. Earth & Sky carries that principle as its message: what we take from the earth, we must give back. That principle extends into how Banke Kuku approaches production. The brand maintains a no-waste policy, finding uses for offcuts rather than discarding them, while its seasonless approach allows pieces to remain part of the collection beyond a single season. Banke Kuku also uses digital printing, which consumes less heat and water than conventional printing methods, and continues to reduce its use of man-made fabrics in favour of more conscious material choices. Its commitment to the natural world extends beyond its collections, including its work with the Nigerian Conservation Foundation and its Re-Green Movement, which supports afforestation and the restoration of Nigeria’s natural environment. sports.title: Bobby Durkin hits game-winner to beat Cincinnati 63-61
sports.description: CINCINNATI, OH - NOVEMBER 09: Minnesota Golden Gophers forward Bobby Durkin (3) reacts with his teammates after making a game-winning three-pointer during the game against the Minnesota Golden Gophers and the Cincinnati Bearcats on November 9, 2026 at Fifth Third Arena in Cincinnati, OH. (Photo by Ian Johnson/Icon Sportswire via Getty Images) | Icon Sportswire via Getty Images After trailing for most of the second half, the Gophers scrambled to come back and Bobby Durkin hit a deep three in the final seconds to beat the Cincinnati Bearcats 63-61 and remain undefeated. Kyan Evans did most of the work throughout the game, scoring 26 points, grabbing 10 rebounds and five assists. But it was Isaac Asuma, advancing the ball to Bobby Durkin, who hit his only three of the game to give Minnesota the lead with 0.4 on the clock and essentially sealing the win for Minnesota. Minnesota jumped out to an early lead and seemed to be controlling the game for the first 10 minutes of the game. But then Cincinnati just slowly took control of the pace of the game, playing good defense and making things difficult for everyone on the Gopher offense except Evans. The Bearcats forced a ton of Gopher turnovers that they turned into points, but Minnesota battled back and Durkin put the nail in the coffin to push the Gophers to 3-0 on the young season. WHY IT MATTERED: The win is great, being 3-0 is great, but this will count as a Quad 1 win for the Gophers and is the best non-conference win since beating North Carolina and West Virginia in back-to-back games in 2011. This is a game that will benefit the Gophers as they try to get back to the NCAA Tournament. GAME BALL: Evans had a double-double and his first big night scoring as a Gopher. But how do you not give the game ball to Bobby Buckets? THE STAT : For Cincinnati, it was turnovers; for the Gophers, it was offensive rebounds. Both were garnering extra possessions for their team and frustrating their fans. Cincy forced 17 turnovers that resulted in 16 points. Minnesota grabbed 13 offensive rebounds that allowed them to score 11 bonus points. TURNING POINT : This one was definitely in favor of the Bearcats, with a 79% chance of winning with 17 seconds left. And then MJ Collins missed the front end of a 1-and-1 and Asuma found Durkin for the game-winner. HOT : Cincinnati’s Tylen Riley has scored 11 points this season, but he was on fire tonight. The senior guard was 8/17 and 6/9 from three to finish with 25 points. NOT : Durkin had just two points and was 0-5 from three this game before he hit the game-winner. He had two threes blocked and looked out-of-sorts for most of this game. UP NEXT: The Gophers get a couple of gimme-games with Southern and Western Illinois coming to the Barn before three straight games against Power 5 teams. Southern is on Thursday at 7:00.

Purdue changes up the starting lineup as you would expect with Antione West Jr. and Jack Benter being slotted in place of Omer Mayer and Gicarri Harris. sports.title: Finally, Purdue basketball finds its offense late to run off Illinois State
sports.description: WEST LAFAYETTE − At last, Purdue basketball fans can breathe a sigh of relief. It took huge late run to blow the game open, but the Boilermakers left Mackey Arena with their first victory. A lineup change that included Jack Benter and Antione West Jr. among the starting helped pilot Purdue 's 76-59 win over Illinois State . Purdue (1-2) led 50-48 midway through the second half before landing the knockout blow it needed after losses to Gonzaga and Valparaiso to open the season while also snapping out of its 3-point shooting funk. After combining to shoot just 20.4% from 3 in the first two games, the Boilers made 8 of 19 against the Redbirds (1-2). Purdue basketball turning point vs. Illinois State Despite a hot shooting first half, Purdue couldn't separate itself from the Redbirds. Illinois State had a chance to cut the lead to two Louie Semona II's 3-pointer was off and Enzo Shahrvin pulled down the rebound. Purdue called timeout to set up a final play. Antione West Jr. ended up making a stepback 3-pointer from the right wing to give the Boilermakers a 36-28 halftime lead. That shot was Purdue's saving grace for a long time, but it was just enough to keep Illinois State from ever pulling even or going ahead. Eventually, Purdue found its footing and blew the game open with a 24-2 run relying on a lineup of Antione West Jr., Luke Ertel, CJ Cox, Jack Benter and Daniel Jacobsen. Game MVP Jack Benter received his first two career starts out of necessity when Trey Kaufman-Renn was sidelined to open last season. On Monday, the junior was in the starting rotation for the first time in a year. He showed what he's capable of from the get go, sinking a 3-pointer for the game's first points, then drawing a charge on the defensive end. It set the stage for a productive night across the board for Benter, who finished with 14 points, 5 rebounds, 3 assists and a steal. 3 Purdue basketball standouts vs. Illinois State Daniel Jacobsen: Three games in a row is a trend. The 7-foot-4 center is Purdue's best offensive piece. It was another stellar night for the Boilermaker big man, contributing his third straight game with at least 20 points, hitting that number on the nose. Jacobsen also had 7 rebounds and 3 assists. Antione West Jr.: In his first career start after sitting out last season, West had a coming out party. West scored 17 points on 7 of 11 shooting and added 2 rebounds, 2 assists and a steal. CJ Cox: The junior guard made three early midrange jumpers. He didn't fill up the stat sheet, but he didn't hurt the Boilermakers either. Cox had 10 points, 3 assists and, in typical Cox fashion, no turnovers. Sam King covers sports for the Journal & Courier. sports.title: Dana White Turns Down Donald Trump’s Press Secretary Offer in Hilarious Exchange at White House

sports.title: Josh Allen has run for 5,000 yards and only 4 other QBs can say that
sports.description: MINNEAPOLIS, MINNESOTA - NOVEMBER 09: Josh Allen #17 of the Buffalo Bills runs the ball for a first down against the Minnesota Vikings during the first quarter of the game at U.S. Bank Stadium on November 09, 2026 in Minneapolis, Minnesota. (Photo by Stephen Maturen/Getty Images) | Getty Images Josh Allen has run for 5,000 yards in the NFL. For a guy whose primary job is throwing the football, that’s a lot of ground covered. The Buffalo Bills quarterback became just the fifth quarterback in NFL history to reach that total during Buffalo’s Week 9 game against the Minnesota Vikings. Allen crossed the 5k mark in the third quarter on a series of designed runs. He entered the game at 4991 then had a 7-yard run in the first quarter to get to 4998. He lost one yard on the kneel down to end the first half to fall back to 4997. A 5-yard scramble from the Minnesota 21 was followed by a 3-yard run to make sure he was over. And counting… Allen joins Lamar Jackson, Michael Vick, Cam Newton, and Russell Wilson in the 5,000-yard group. That’s the entire list, and Allen has put himself on it in his ninth NFL season. Bills fans have watched those yards come a few different ways. There have been scrambles after the protection breaks down, designed runs, and more than a few plays where Allen decides the best way to get a first down is to go through whoever is standing in front of him. They all count. Of course, if he slid more often, like we all keep screaming for him to do, it would have taken a few more carries to get there. Allen already owns the NFL record for career rushing touchdowns by a quarterback. Now he has another number to go with it, and another reminder of how much of Buffalo’s offense has come from his legs.

technology.title: Cisco to link all future products to its SaaS-y Cloud Control management tool
technology.description: Cisco will no longer create products that don’t integrate with Cloud Control, its SaaS-y management platform that offers netadmins a single tool to manage all of the networking giant’s devices and much of its software portfolio. The networking giant announced Cloud Control in June 2025 and only made it available to customers in the USA. Cisco has previously told The Register that slow rollout reflects the fact that Cisco needs to nail privacy and other regulatory niceties, and deploy infrastructure, before introducing the service to other markets. It appears Cisco is now satisfied it has sorted out those issues. Jeff Schultz, Cisco’s senior vice president for portfolio strategy and marketing, today told the company’s Live conference in Australia that Cloud Control will come online in the European Union, UK, and Down Under in February 2027. Japan, India, and Canada will get their turn in May. Schultz said Cisco is “working tirelessly” to deploy Cloud Control across the world as soon as possible. He also revealed that, starting next year, Cisco will no longer ship products that don’t integrate with Cloud Control. That doesn’t mean those products will be manageable only if they can connect to Cloud Control. Instead, the decision reflects Cisco’s belief that the main thing stopping its customers buying more of its products is the complexity of operating them in concert. Schultz also feels that Cloud Control represents “platform advantage” for Cisco, because when users integrate networking, security, and observability the result is better manageability and resilience. Schultz also told the conference that Cisco will bundle its Thousand Eyes observability and security tool with the “Essentials” and “Advantage” licenses. “We admit it was hard to license and deploy,” he said during his keynote speech, adding that the tool will be deployed automatically with Wi‑Fi 6E and Wi‑Fi 7 hardware. Another product Cisco plans to bring to more customers is Live Protect, a tool that implements compensating controls for flaws that organizations can’t immediately patch. Live Protect currently works on some switches, plus SD-WAN and WLAN controllers. From December, Cisco will extend it to 8000 series routers, secure firewalls, campus gateway, and to Cloud Control itself. From May 2027, Live Protect will work with Cisco’s ASR 9000 series service aggregation routers and Network Convergence System. ®

science.title: Global carbon emissions set to fall in 2026 due to Iran energy shock
science.description: The blockade of the Strait of Hormuz led to a spike in oil prices Anna Ivanova/Alamy Carbon dioxide emissions from fossil fuels are expected to drop this year for the first time in five years. The slowdown has been partly attributed to the energy shock triggered by the US and Israel’s war on Iran. The conflict, which began in February, led to a jump in oil prices after the Strait of Hormuz, the main trade route for about 20 per cent of the world’s oil and liquefied natural gas, was blockaded by Iran in response. This is still affecting petrol prices and household gas bills, and has seen countries around the world turn to alternative fuel types to boost energy security. Advertisement Read more Solar energy is going to power the world much sooner than you think Around 38.2 gigatonnes of CO2 are expected to be emitted in 2026 globally, according to the latest annual Global Carbon Budget – put together by more than 140 researchers. This is a 0.4 per cent decrease on the previous year, largely due to a projected 1.9 per cent fall in emissions from oil. The drop in oil use was partly offset by a 0.6 per cent increase in emissions from coal. Robbie Andrew at climate research group CICERO in Oslo, Norway, one of the report authors, says financial pressures due to the energy shock are likely to have caused the drop in emissions this year, which may turn out to be a “blip”. “On the assumption that there are no further crises, then you’d expect that emissions would bounce back,” says Andrew. The two biggest dips in emissions in the 21st century have been attributed to the covid-19 pandemic, which saw emissions drop by around 6 per cent in 2020, and the global financial crisis, which saw emissions drop around 2 per cent in 2009. The future outlook depends on how long the energy shock lasts, says Andrew, with governments forced to look at the economic case for continuing to subsidise fossil fuels. The rollout of renewable energy also played a part in bringing down carbon emissions. Electric vehicles and solar and wind power are predicted to offset 64 to 79 per cent of increasing emissions from demand growth through to 2028. Free newsletter Sign up to The Earth Edition Sign up to newsletter In China, the world’s biggest emitter of CO2, emissions are projected to decrease by 0.9 per cent in 2026 as the country continues to make strides with expanding renewable energy and electric vehicles. “What’s keeping emissions down is the renewable energy, and the price of oil actually suppresses this even more,” says Corinne Le Quéré at the University of East Anglia, UK, who also worked on the report. “So, that’s encouraging in a way, but it does mean that if the price of oil rebounds to pre-Iran [conflict] levels, most likely the emissions will rebound as well until we have enough further acceleration in renewable energy to really bring the emissions down durably.” Journal Reference: Nature Climate Change DOI: 10.1038/s41558-026-02821-8

NASA/JPL-Caltech Written by Roger C. Wiens, SuperCam Principal Investigator for NASA’s Perseverance rover at Purdue University Nov. 4, 2026 Exploration on Mars turns up the unexpected. Perseverance is equipped with a fantastic set of instruments for studying the rock record of this ancient planet. Both PIXL and SuperCam have great capabilities for detecting all kinds of elements. SHERLOC, SuperCam, and PIXL can detect minerals using various techniques including x-ray fluorescence, Raman, and infrared spectroscopies. As a side benefit of the way SuperCam performs its Raman spectroscopy, it can also study time-resolved luminescence. Normally luminescence occurs over a broad wavelength range (most of Earth’s commercial lighting uses luminescence in some way or another). Two years ago, the SuperCam team was startled to find strong, narrow luminescence peaks at two wavelengths of 692.7 and 694.1 nanometers when they shot a light-colored rock with the laser. This luminescence comes from delayed atomic transitions in chromium atoms present in a corundum mineral structure. SuperCam can time the delay of the atomic transitions via the resulting photons, and so we could verify that this emission came from chromium in corundum. The results were published in Geophysical Research Letters by a team led by Ann Ollila earlier this year, so you can read all about it. The gemstone version of chromium-containing corundum is ruby. Prior to installing SuperCam on Perseverance, we placed a ruby in the laser beam and watched the entire room pulse a brilliant red as SuperCam’s laser beam hit the gemstone; it was extremely bright. While we haven’t found collectable rubies on Mars yet, the little corundum crystals are helping us learn more about Mars’ past. Corundum is a metamorphic and pegmatitic mineral which we would not expect to find on Mars, a planet that lacks plate tectonics. However, large meteor and asteroid impacts can create local metamorphism due to long-term heating from the impact. Because we are in a very ancient terrain near the rim of Jezero crater, we can expect some evidence of localized metamorphism. As the first mission in such terrain, we are learning new things. NASA/JPL-Caltech/ASU Written by Tasha Coelho, Mastcam-Z Student Collaborator at Arizona State University Nov. 1, 2026 Perseverance’s most recent abrasion “Pumbe” bears a striking resemblance to an earlier abrasion, “ Badger Peak .” That’s no coincidence. As previously reported , that rock had a hardness too high to core. However, the team felt strongly that it was worth the effort to add a gabbro, an igneous rock made mostly of calcium-rich plagioclase feldspar and pyroxene crystals, to Perseverance’s sample collection . In search of a new local gabbroic candidate to sample, Perseverance traveled about 100 meters (330 feet) to a different patch of light-toned rocks . Indeed, visual and chemical data from the light-toned rocks in the new workspace revealed a composition similar to that of “Badger Peak.” NASA’s Mars Perseverance rover acquired this image of the abrasion patch “Pumbe” using its SHERLOC WATSON camera, located on the turret at the end of the rover’s robotic arm. The image was acquired on Oct. 17, 2026 (Sol 2011), at a local mean solar time of 16:14:35. The abrasion patch is about 5 centimeters (2 inches) across. NASA/JPL-Caltech To improve the odds of collecting a sample this time, the team made prudent decisions: choosing a neighboring rock with a flatter surface better oriented for the drill stabilizers to press against, and using a coring bit with less wear. At last, in a display of the rover’s namesake quality, the drill made it about 3.1 centimeters (1.2 inches) into the rock. Sample acquisition activities followed, making “Singita” the rover’s first sample in more than a year. While Singita is the newest sample, it may be among the oldest rocks in Perseverance’s collection . Textures in the rock suggest that it likely formed deep in the crust and was modified and excavated by at least one, and possibly multiple, large impact events. Perseverance has now completed its 66 th successful abrasion and collected an intriguing new sample alongside it. science.title: On this day in space! Nov. 9, 1967: NASA launches the Saturn V moon rocket for the first time on Apollo 4, but no astronauts were aboard
science.description: null On Nov. 9, 1967, NASA launched the powerful new Saturn V rocket on its maiden voyage. The Saturn V moon rocket was 363 feet tall. That's taller than the Statue of Liberty! It was the biggest and most powerful rocket ever built at the time (though SpaceX's Starship megarocket has since surpassed it). NASA needed such a powerful rocket to launch astronauts to the moon. However, the first Saturn V launch didn't carry astronauts, because it was only a test flight. During the launch, the rocket created a loud shockwave that surprised nearby observers. The ground shook so hard that it rattled buildings miles away, and all the shaking caused a huge shower of dust and debris NASA's new launch center, the Kennedy Space Center in Florida. The mission lasted 8 hours 36 minutes. The rocket carried an uncrewed command module that splashed down in the Pacific Ocean. NASA's first-ever Saturn V rocket launches on its maiden flight from Cape Canaveral, Florida on the uncrewed Apollo 4 test flight on Nov. 9, 1967. (Image credit: NASA) Why it mattered The launch of Apollo 4 in November 1967 was a turning point for NASA on its path to landing astronauts on the moon. The space agency had bet the moon on its new Saturn V booster, a three-stage heavy-lift rocket designed to fly astronauts in a capsule (as well as their lander) to the moon and back. But the rocket had never been fully tested until the Apollo 4 launch. NASA also needed a new launch site for its Apollo missions. So the agency built Launch Complex 39 at what is now called the Kennedy Space Center, a Florida spaceport that has become the home port for orbital human spaceflight in the United States. But in 1967, no rockets had ever flown from the site. Yet, everything went according to plan. Amazing Apollo 4: NASA's 1st Saturn V Moon Rocket Test Flight in Photos “It was really an expert launching all the way through from lifting off exactly on time to performance of every single stage,” rocket pioneer Wernher von Braun , director of NASA’s Marshall Space Flight Center in Huntsville, Alabama, said at the time . The launch came as NASA was on its heels. Just months earlier, on Jan. 27, 1967, the space agency suffered a fatal tragedy when Apollo 1 astronauts Gus Grissom, Ed White and Roger Chaffee died on the launch pad after a fire broke out inside their Apollo command module during a ground test. A view of the Apollo 4 launch after stage separation looking back down at Earth from the Saturn V rocket. NASA/Interm Archives/Getty The uncrewed Apollo 4 command module splashes down under parachutes after a smooth test flight. NASA/Interm Archives/Getty “The maiden voyage of the Saturn V dramatically increased the confidence of people across the nation in the management of the largest research and development undertaking in which the western world has ever engaged,” George Mueller, NASA's then-Associate Administrator for Manned Space Flight, said at the time . science.title: Jupiter and Mars are set for a breathtaking close approach later this week: Here's how to see it
science.description: null Jupiter and Mars will shine side by side in a spectacular close approach in the heart of the constellation Leo on Nov. 15. Here's what you need to know. Mars and Jupiter reach their closest apparent separation in Earth's sky at 9:04 p.m. EST on Nov. 15 (0204 GMT on Nov. 16), according to astronomy website In-The-Sky . The planets will be below the horizon for U.S. stargazers at the moment of their closest approach, but observers can catch the pair rising above the eastern horizon around midnight local time, just a few hours later. Remember: You can discover the exact timings for the rising and setting of the planets above your local horizon using Time and Date's night sky tracker . Jupiter will be the brightest of the pair, when it rises a little over 1 degree from the red light of Mars — roughly the width of your little finger held at arm's length against the night sky. The bright star Regulus will glow close at hand, forming the dot of the backward question mark formation of stars that represents the head of the great Lion in the constellation Leo. Celestron StarSense Explorer LT114AZ (Image credit: Celestron) The Celestron StarSense Explorer LT114AZ is a great way to get a closer look at Jupiter, Mars and Saturn. Its 4.5-inch aperture and a high 1000mm focal length delivers good magnification out of the box, plus it's integrated with the StarSense smartphone app, which makes finding those planets so much easier. Check out our full review for more. Mars and Jupiter will be close enough to share the field of view of a pair of 10x50 binoculars and will also make for a spectacular sight through the eyepiece of a telescope when viewed separately as they rise away from the horizon. The gas giant's iconic Great Red Spot will rotate into view in the predawn hours of Nov. 16, and will be visible through a backyard telescope with an aperture of just 4 inches . Using a light green color filter will help increase the visibility of the vast storm, while an orange filter will help bring out detail in the gas giant's sweeping cloud belts. The two planets will appear to gradually drift apart over the coming weeks and won't appear as close again for another 2.5 years in July 2029 , when the two planets appear close together in the constellation Virgo . Be sure to check out our guide to photographing the night sky , along with our picks of the best cameras and lenses for astrophotography if you're interested in following the dance of the planets for yourself. science.title: Are the James Webb Space Telescope's mysterious Little Red Dots actually tiny black holes left over from the Big Bang era?
science.description: null Ever since NASA's James Webb Space Telescope (JWST) started observing the early universe, it has been providing almost as many surprises as it has answers. One such surprise are the so-called Little Red Dots, cosmic objects that seemingly disappear completely before the universe is two billion years old. New research suggests that Little Red Dots may actually be connected primordial black holes , tiny black holes born not from dying stars but rather from fluctuations in the density of matter just after the Big Bang, in the earliest moments of cosmic history. Should they exist, primordial black holes would predate stars, galactic dust particles, and elements heavier than hydrogen and helium. Now, researchers have used JWST data to test whether one particular Little Red Dot, known as blackAbell 2744-QSO1 (QSO1), could host a primordial black hole. "A black hole is an object born from the gravitational death of a star. Primordial black holes are a very different story," study team member Valerio De Luca, of the Department of Physics and Astronomy at Johns Hopkins University (JHU) in Maryland, said in a statement . "They come from the physics of the early universe that predates the first stars, when the universe was expanding exponentially in time and space. So the mechanisms for creating primordial black holes are different," De Luca added. Little Red Dots could be the smoking gun of primordial black holes Though scientists have theorized about the existence of primordial black holes since they were first proposed by Stephen Hawking in the 1970s, no hard evidence has presented itself. One of the issues scientists have puzzled over is how to tell the difference between a primordial black hole and a "traditional" or astrophysical black hole formed from the supernova death and collapse of a massive star. "Little Red Dots could surround astrophysical black holes, and most probably many of them do, but they could also be primordial black holes, if primordial black holes exist," De Luca said. "So the question becomes, Which ones are primordial and how can we tell?" De Luca and colleagues turned their attention to QS01, located around 13.1 billion light-years from Earth, which is seen as it was just 700 million years after the Big Bang. What makes this Little Red Dot stand out is the fact that it is almost entirely composed of hydrogen and helium. Because these were the universe's first elements, it could be more unspoiled and primordial than other Little Red Dots. The team modeled how a Little Red Dot like QS01 could form from a primordial black hole. That was necessary because the circumstances under which this could happen would have to be very specific. "There are constraints on primordial black holes from cosmological observations," said team member Loris Del Grosso, also of JHU's Department of Physics and Astronomy. science.title: NYT bestseller ‘Robopocalypse’ is getting a TV series with Oscar winners Ron Howard and Akiva Goldsman at the helm
science.description: null They say all good things come to those who wait… and WAIT. Well, the wait for "Robopocalypse" fans might finally be over, as Oscar winners Ron Howard and Akiva Goldsman have announced they're working on a TV adaptation. It does seem like an eternity since news first broke that Portland-based New York Times bestselling author Daniel H. Wilson’s "Robopocalypse" (Doubleday, 2011) was bought by Steven Spielberg’s DreamWorks SKG for a sci-fi spectacle, with Drew Goddard ("The Martian") brought in to pen the screenplay. That was back in 2009, and since then the story of a rogue AI named Archos and a hearty band of indigenous people in America’s heartland battling to save humanity from extinction has been placed on Hollywood’s back burner. After numerous stalled starts and director Michael Bay getting involved in 2018, "Robopocalypse" was quietly powered down due to script issues, filmmaker scheduling conflicts, and the enormous budget required. But now we have been blessed with the news , first broken by The Hollywood Reporter, that Ron Howard ("Apollo 13," "The Da Vinci Code") and Akiva Goldsman ("A Beautiful Mind," "Star Trek: Strange New Worlds") have taken up the mantle of this chilling sci-fi project to develop as a new TV series. And what timing, just as AI fever has gripped the planet with paranoia centered around our eventual robot overlords. "'Robopocalypse' has all the scale and suspense of a major action story, but what drew me to it are the thought-provoking themes and humanity at its center," Ron Howard shared in a statement. The cover of 2011's smash sci-fi hit Robopocalypse by Daniel H. Wilson Vintage The cover of the 2014 sequel Robogenesis by Daniel H. Wilson Vintage "Daniel created a future that feels both startling and increasingly plausible, with characters who must figure out what connects us when the technology we rely on turns against us. I am also thrilled to work with Akiva again. We have shared some incredibly meaningful creative experiences, and this feels like the right story to bring us back together." As a PhD graduate of Carnegie Mellon University’s Robotics Institute and a future king of the techno-thriller, Wilson was the ideal writer to bring this frightening story to life, and a 2014 sequel titled "Robogenesis" was equally gripping. The prolific, award-winning writer has since set up a multitude of other Hollywood projects spawned from his catalog of works, including "Amped," "The Clockwork Dynasty," the authorized sequel to Michael Crichton's "The Andromeda Strain," " The Andromeda Evolution ," and his 2025 alien invasion novel "Hole in the Sky," still alive at Netflix. science.title: NASA’s Chandra Finds Source of Star’s Mysterious Outbursts
science.description: A composite NASA Chandra X-ray and Sloan Digital Sky Survey (SDSS) optical image of the galaxy NGC 4559 located about 30 million light-years from Earth. The Chandra data shows X-ray point sources represented in purple, and the SDSS data shows the galaxy and foreground and background objects in red and blue. The luminous blue variable and supernova impostor AT 2016blu is in the middle of the small square. X-ray: NASA/CXC/Univ. of Virgina/M. Aghakhanloo et al.; Optical: SDSS; Image Processing: NASA/CXC/SAO/P. Edmonds Using NASA’s Chandra X-ray Observatory, astronomers have discovered what is triggering repeated outbursts from a giant, unstable star. A new study , published Monday in the latest issue of The Astrophysical Journal, details the discovery of a previously hidden companion object that keeps pulling material away from the massive star every 113 days as they orbit one another. This partner is either a stellar-mass black hole, or the dense collapsed core of a massive star called a neutron star. This is the first X-ray detection of one of this class of erupting stars. It is also the first of these objects found with a black hole or neutron star companion. The volatile star, known as AT 2016blu, is in the spiral galaxy NGC 4559, located about 30 million light-years from Earth. Astronomers estimate the mass of this star is at least 33 times that of the Sun. “For 15 years, astronomers have been watching this star get really bright and then dim again on a regular basis,” said Mojgan Aghakhanloo of the University of Virginia in Charlottesville, who led this study. “Until we were able to get Chandra data at the right time, we couldn’t figure out what was making this happen.” The star AT 2016blu is a type of luminous blue variable, which are hot, massive stars characterized by changes in brightness. Eta Carinae, for example, is a particularly well-known luminous blue variable.) AT 2016blu is a special type of luminous blue variable that undergoes rapid and repeated increases in brightness. The spikes in brightness are so extreme that they resemble supernova explosions, where a massive star collapses onto itself and material then hurtles outward into space. However, unlike in a supernova explosion, the star is not destroyed, so AT 2016blu is also referred to as a “supernova impostor.” Between 2012 and 2026, astronomers detected at least 27 bursts of optical light, or light in wavelengths that are visible to our eyes, from AT 2016blu roughly every 113 days. “This star’s behavior was confusing at first because it kept acting like a supernova, but clearly it’s not because it keeps surviving these outbursts about three times a year,” said co-author Núria Torres-Albà, also of the University of Virginia. “To understand the cause of these eruptions, we realized we needed X-ray data, timed so that we’d observe the star when it was in an outburst.” The team used Chandra because it is the only X-ray telescope with sharp enough vision to distinguish AT 2016blu

science.title: Starfish Space loses contact with 1st 'Otter' servicing spacecraft, ending NASA tech-demo mission
science.description: null Starfish Space's first Otter has died, just a month after it reached the final frontier. The Seattle startup announced on Tuesday (Nov. 3) that its Otter 24C satellite suffered a glitch in low Earth orbit (LEO) and is not recoverable. The anomaly killed an ambitious mission in the cradle, as Otter 24C was still in the commissioning phase. Otter 24C launched Oct. 1 on SpaceX 's Transporter-18 mission, a rideshare flight that carried a total of 130 payloads to LEO (including a prototype satellite for Project Suncatcher , Google's planned AI constellation). The Starfish satellite was flying a mission for NASA called Small Spacecraft Propulsion and Inspection Capability, or SSPICY for short. The goal was to "demonstrate technologies necessary for future debris-removal missions as well as for future applications in the servicing and inspection of active spacecraft," according to NASA's SSPICY site . "This advances NASA's in-space manufacturing and assembly (ISAM) goals to ensure a sustainable space operating environment and builds towards a future where objects can be assembled, repaired and maintained in space, significantly expanding possibilities for science and human exploration," the agency added. Starfish Space was a natural partner. The Seattle company plans to become a big player in the nascent field of satellite servicing , using its line of Otter craft to repair, refuel or deorbit other satellites for a variety of customers. Illustration of a Starfish Space Otter satellite rendesvousing with another spacecraft in Earth orbit. (Image credit: Starfish Space) SSPICY marked Otter's spaceflight debut. The mission plan called for the 739-pound (335-kilogram) Otter 24C spacecraft to approach and inspect "up to four inoperable space objects of U.S. origin" over the course of a two-year mission, performing detailed visual inspections. But Otter 24C never got the chance to perform any of these orbital rendezvous. "While working through commissioning steps, Starfish eventually stopped receiving data from Otter 24C," the company said in a Nov. 3 X post . And there's $1 million in prizes up for grabs for the winners. To build and sustain a base on the moon , NASA will have to solve a myriad of problems. And they're looking to the next generation for help, the space agency's chief Jared Isaacman said Sunday (Nov. 8). "We are inviting students from across the country to help solve some of the problems that stand between humanity and a permanent presence on another world," Isaacman said. "We're putting 1 million in prizes together to support the best ideas and recognize the teams behind them." Isaacman made this announcement wearing his blue flight suit from the rocket garden at NASA's Kennedy Space Center Visitor Center amidst the agency's MAX POWER air show event . Just the day before, he flew fighter jets in that suit and even jumped out of a plane, skydiving into the event. Soon after this announcement, he was flying another fighter plane above the crowd. The audience for this announcement was filled with students of all ages. Some young children wearing costume spacesuits squeezed as close as they could to the front of the room while teenagers considering their futures listened intently. It was clear that Isaacman's presence and words were landing with this group. But what moon base challenges does NASA want to see these students tackle? In short, all of them. "The moon base will allow us to conduct groundbreaking science, test new technologies, and prepare again for where we inevitably go next, which is the red planet," he said.
